period: c. 2600 BCE – 1900 BCE (Mature Phase); c. 3300 – 1300 BCE (Overall)

significance.en: First European explorer to visit Harappa mounds; documented ruins in 'Narrative of Various Journeys in Balochistan, Afghanistan and the Panjab'.
significance.hi: हड़प्पा के टीलों का दौरा करने वाले प्रथम यूरोपीय यात्री; अपनी पुस्तक में खंडहरों का प्रथम अभिलेखीकरण किया।

significance.en: Father of Indian Archaeology; surveyed Harappa; acquired first Indus seal (hump-less bull motif) but failed to realize its antiquity.
significance.hi: भारतीय पुरातत्व के जनक; हड़प्पा का सर्वेक्षण किया; प्रथम सिन्धु मुहर (बिना कूबड़ वाला वृषभ) प्राप्त की।

significance.en: Brunton brothers used ancient Harappan baked bricks as track ballast while laying the Lahore-Karachi railway line.
significance.hi: लाहौर-कराची रेलवे लाइन बिछाते समय ब्रंटन बंधुओं ने गिट्टी के रूप में प्राचीन हड़प्पा कालीन पकी ईंटों का उपयोग किया।

significance.en: First scientific excavation at Harappa (Montgomery/Sahiwal, Punjab, Pakistan) under ASI Director Sir John Marshall.
significance.hi: सर जॉन मार्शल के निर्देशन में हड़प्पा का प्रथम वैज्ञानिक उत्खनन प्रारम्भ किया।

significance.en: Discovered Mohenjo-daro (Larkana, Sindh) while investigating a 2nd century CE Kushana Buddhist stupa mound.
significance.hi: कुषाण कालीन बौद्ध स्तूप टीले की खोज करते हुए मोहनजोदड़ो की खोज की।

significance.en: Officially announced the discovery of a new Bronze Age civilization to the world in 'The Illustrated London News'; coined term 'Indus Civilization'.
significance.hi: 'द इलस्ट्रेटेड लंदन न्यूज' में विश्व के समक्ष सिन्धु घाटी सभ्यता की ऐतिहासिक घोषणा की; 'सिन्धु सभ्यता' नामकरण किया।

geographicalLimits.shape: Triangular (~1.3 million sq. km / 12,99,600 sq km - larger than contemporary Egypt & Mesopotamia combined)

limits.river: Pravara River (tributary of Godavari / प्रवरा नदी)
Hindon River (tributary of Yamuna / हिण्डन नदी)

specialOutposts.importance: Trading colony for Lapis Lazuli procurement; only site with direct evidence of canal irrigation

majorSitesTable.excavator: D.R. Sahni (1921), M.S. Vats (1926), Mortimer Wheeler (1946)
keyFindings: 12 Granaries in 2 rows of 6 each outside the citadel
18 circular brick threshing floors with traces of wheat and barley husk
Barracks / workmen quarters (labour accommodation)
Cemetery R-37 and Cemetery H (post-Harappan culture)
Coffin burial made of scented Elm/Rosewood
Red sandstone torso of a nude dancing youth (Greco-Roman naturalism precursor)
Grey stone male torso with socket holes for movable limbs
Single-room tenements for workmen near the granaries
Copper bullock cart (Ikka), bronze mirror, vanity box

majorSitesTable.excavator: R.D. Banerjee (1922), Sir John Marshall, Ernest Mackay (1927), Wheeler (1947)
keyFindings: Great Bath (11.88 m x 7.01 m x 2.43 m) lined with bitumen/gypsum mortar for ritual purification
Great Granary (45.71 m x 15.23 m) - largest single architectural monument in Mohenjo-daro
Assembly Hall / Collegiate Hall (multi-pillared building with 20 brick pillars)
Bronze Dancing Girl (Lost-wax / cire perdue technique, 10.5 cm, right arm on hip, bangles up to shoulder)
Steatite Bearded Priest-King (draped in trefoil-embroidered shawl over left shoulder)
Pashupati Mahadeva Seal (3-faced horned deity surrounded by Elephant, Tiger, Rhino, Buffalo + 2 deers at feet)
Piece of woven cotton cloth adhering to the silver lid of a vase (earliest cotton fabric)
Clay model of a boat / masted ship
Cylindrical seal of Mesopotamian origin (proof of Persian Gulf / Sumerian trade)
Over 700 private and public brick wells across city quarters
Absence of Cemetery (unlike Harappa, Mohenjo-daro had no formal cemetery; fractional burials found in rooms)

majorSitesTable.river: Bhogava (tributary of Sabarmati, Gulf of Khambhat)
keyFindings: Tidal Dockyard (world's oldest artificial brick dock basin: 214 m x 36 m with sluice gate)
Rice husk impressions in pottery matrix (earliest rice evidence along with Rangpur)
Bead-making factory with working platform, raw agate stones and circular kiln
Persian Gulf button seal (circular steatite seal with two gazelles flanking a four-rayed motif)
Joint / Double burial (3 graves with two skeletons buried together - male and female)
Terracotta model of a horse and terracotta mummy-like figurine
Ivory linear measurement scale (division unit ~1.7 mm, smallest recorded in Bronze Age)
Row of Fire Altars (Yajna-kundas) in both citadel and lower town
Painted jar depicting the 'Cunning Fox and Thirsty Crow' fable (Panchatantra precursor)
Citadel and Lower Town enclosed within a single rectangular perimeter wall (no internal partition!)

majorSitesTable.excavator: A. Ghosh (1953), B.B. Lal & B.K. Thapar (1961)
keyFindings: Ploughed field surface with criss-cross furrows (world's earliest evidence of mixed cropping: mustard & chickpea)
Row of 7 Fire Altars on raised mud-brick platforms with ash, charcoal and animal bones
Camel bones (earliest domestic camel evidence in South Asia)
Both Citadel and Lower Town fortified separately with substantial mud-brick defensive walls
Decorative tiled floor with interlocking circles pattern
Wooden furrow / plough traces in pre-Harappan levels
Evidence of earliest earthquake (~2600 BCE causing abandonment of early settlement)
Absence of covered drainage system along streets (household soak pits used instead)
Mud-brick residential architecture instead of baked brick (Wheeler called it 'poor settlement')

majorSitesTable.river: Mansar and Manhar seasonal streams (Luni basin)
keyFindings: Unique Tripartite City Planning: Divided into 3 distinct walled sectors (Citadel, Middle Town, Lower Town)
Gigantic stone-cut water reservoirs: 16 cascading check dams and rock-cut cisterns storing ~250,000 cu. m water
Harappan Signboard / Inscription: 10 large white gypsum Indus signs (~37 cm high) mounted on wooden board at North Gate
Monumental stone architecture using finely dressed white sandstone blocks (precursor to Mauryan stone polish)
Grand stadium / ceremonial ground (283 m long) for state festivals and sports between citadel and middle town
Free-standing polished stone pillars and monolithic stone water channels
UNESCO World Heritage Site declared in 2021
Largest Harappan site in the world (>350–550 hectares, spanning 9 mounds - larger than Mohenjo-daro)
Ancient DNA Study (Narasimhan & Shinde, Cell 2019): Verified indigenous ancestry; absence of Steppe pastoralist DNA in Mature IVC
Granary complex, multi-room houses, terracotta drainage pipes, paved streets
Gold and lapis lazuli manufacturing workshop with unworked ores and crucibles
11 female burials with ornate shell bangles, copper mirrors and agate beads

location.en: Nawabshah, Sindh, Pakistan (130 km south of Mohenjo-daro)

keyFindings: ONLY Indus city WITHOUT A CITADEL (completely unfortified industrial settlement)
Specialized bead-making factory with furnaces, drills and steatite micro-beads
Lipstick / lip-colour cosmetic traces and small cosmetic toilet kits
Bronze toy cart and bullock cart models with movable drivers
Mud-brick with imprinted footprint of a dog chasing a cat
Inkpot / ink-well for writing or calligraphy
Seal-cutting and shell-working workshops
Clay model of a plough (complete terracotta toy plough)
Highest quality of two-row Barley grains recovered anywhere in Harappan civilization
Radial / semi-circular street layout (star-shaped streets radiating from citadel gate, not strict gridiron)
Absence of systematic covered drainage (drainage soak jars used instead)
Deep defensive moat encircling the citadel fortification wall
Evidence of both Pre-Harappan, Mature Harappan and Late Harappan phases
Horse skeletal remains / equine bones (identified by Hungarian archaeozoologist Sandor Bokonyi)
Pot burial system: 4 oval pits covered with massive stone slabs
Massive stone rubble fortification wall with mud-brick backing and bastion gateway
First Harappan site excavated in Independent India after Partition (1953)
Human skeleton buried underneath a domestic dog skeleton (Burzahom Neolithic parallel)
Steatite seal, copper celt axe, terracotta ornaments and chert weights
Southernmost outpost of Indus Valley Civilization
Spectacular Bronze Sculpture Hoard: Solid cast bronze chariot pulled by 2 bulls with charioteer, Water buffalo, Elephant, Rhinoceros (total weight ~65 kg cire perdue bronze)
Westernmost boundary post of Indus Valley Civilization
Fortified seaport citadel built on natural rock with massive 30-ft stone wall; key trading node for Mesopotamia
Pre-Harappan to Mature Harappan transition site
Settlement destroyed twice by massive conflagration / fire; pottery decorated with horned deity and fish-scale motifs
Antelope and gazelle bone remains; Rhinoceros skeletal fragments
Key stratigraphy proving transition from rural pre-Harappan Amri culture to urban Harappan phase
Earliest evidence of Rice husk in pottery matrix (along with Lothal)
Lustrous Red Ware pottery; complete absence of Mother Goddess figurines and seals
Major coastal port and manufacturing center for marine Shell (chank) bangles and shell inlay objects

majorSitesTable.river: Confluence of Malir & Bazar streams near Arabian Sea
keyFindings: Smallest Harappan settlement excavated (rural agricultural village: 1.4 hectares)
Hoard of exquisite gold, silver, carnelian ornaments and bronze belt pins in an earthen pot
Trading colony exclusively established for Lapis Lazuli extraction from Badakhshan mines
Traces of engineered irrigation canals in Harappan context; Camel and horse figurines
Northern caravan trade station connecting Indus Valley to Central Asian and Iranian plateau cultures
Two royal silver crowns / tiaras with silver ornaments (earliest silver discovery in Indian subcontinent)
Pre-Harappan settlement with pit-dwellings and copper arrowheads
World's earliest archaeological evidence of Garlic (Lahsun), Ginger (Adrak) and Fenugreek (Methi) cultivation
Oldest excavated Harappan site (~7500–7000 BCE Hakra Ware period, predating Mehrgarh ceramics)
Graffiti of Dancing Girl engraved on potsherd identical to Mohenjo-daro bronze dancing girl posture

significance.en: Easternmost boundary site of Indus Valley Civilization. Yielded cloth impressions on a terracotta trough, faience bangles, ceramic animal figurines, but complete absence of seals and mother goddess figurines.
significance.hi: हड़प्पा सभ्यता का सबसे पूर्वी स्थल। मिट्टी की नाद पर सूती कपड़े की छाप, फ़ाइऑन्स की चूड़ियां व पशु आकृतियां मिलीं; मुहरों एवं मातृदेवी मूर्तियों का पूर्ण अभाव।

significance.en: Remarkable evidence of 5 crops: Wheat, Barley, Rice, Ragi, and Green Gram (Moong). Yielded a non-script sealing impression and mud-brick structures.
significance.hi: 5 फसलों के स्पष्ट प्रमाण: गेहूं, जौ, चावल, रागी व मूंग। गैर-लिपि युक्त मुहर छाप व कच्ची ईंटों की संरचनाएं प्राप्त हुईं।

significance.en: Site of accidental discovery of a massive hoard of Harappan gold jewellery, hollow spacer beads, micro-beads, silver discs, and copper vessels unearthed in an agricultural field.
significance.hi: खेत की जुताई में विशाल स्वर्ण आभूषण, खोखले मणके, सूक्ष्म मणके, चांदी के सिक्के/चकतियां और ताम्र बर्तनों का ऐतिहासिक खजाना प्राप्त हुआ।

upSitesSpecial.phase: Late Harappan / Copper Hoard Transition (c. 2000–1800 BCE)

significance.en: Largest Harappan necropolis in South Asia with 125+ burials. Discovered world's earliest copper-plated solid-wheel royal war chariots, copper antennae swords with anthropomorphic hilts, warrior shields, copper helmets, and ornate wooden coffins with copper inlays.
significance.hi: 125+ कब्रों वाला दक्षिण एशिया का सबसे बड़ा कब्रिस्तान। तांबे से मढ़े युद्ध रथ (चैरियट), तांबे की एंटीनी तलवारें, योद्धा ढालें, ताम्र मुकुट और ताम्र-पर्ण जड़ित शाही लकड़ी के ताबूत प्राप्त हुए।

upSitesSpecial.phase: Late Harappan with Ochre Coloured Pottery (OCP) overlap

significance.en: Shows direct stratigraphic contact between Late Harappan painted ceramic traditions and indigenous Copper Hoard / OCP culture.
significance.hi: उत्तर हड़प्पा कालीन चित्रित मृद्भांड व गैरिक मृद्भांड (OCP) संस्कृति के प्रत्यक्ष संकर साक्ष्य।

source.en: Khetri Mines (Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan - Ganeshwar culture) & Oman (Magan)
Kolar & Hatti Mines (Karnataka), Anantapur (AP) & Indus river gravel sands
source.hi: कोलार व हट्टी की खानें (कर्नाटक) एवं सिन्धु नदी की रेत
जावर की खानें (उदयपुर, राजस्थान), अफगानिस्तान व ईरान
पामीर पर्वत, खोतान एवं मध्य एशिया
नागेश्वर (कच्छ की खाड़ी) एवं बालाकोट (बलूचिस्तान तट)

declineTheoriesTable.proponents: Sir Mortimer Wheeler, Gordon Childe, Stuart Piggott

basisAndRefutation.en: Cited Rigvedic Indra as 'Purandara' (fort-destroyer) and Mohenjo-daro street skeletons. REFUTED: Kenneth Kennedy and George Dales proved skeletons show anemia/malaria, not combat trauma; chronological gap of 300+ years between IVC decline (1900 BCE) and Vedic entry (1500 BCE).
basisAndRefutation.hi: ऋग्वेद में इंद्र को 'पुरंदर' (किलों का ध्वंसक) कहे जाने व मोहनजोदड़ो में कंकालों पर आधारित। खंडन: केनेथ केनेडी ने सिद्ध किया कि कंकाल मलेरिया/एनीमिया से ग्रस्त थे, युद्ध के घाव नहीं; कालक्रम में 300+ वर्षों का अंतर।

basisAndRefutation.en: Massive consumption of timber for firing millions of baked bricks, heating kilns, and domestic hearths depleted forest cover; overgrazing destroyed semi-arid soil stability, causing desertification.
basisAndRefutation.hi: करोड़ों पकी ईंटें पकाने हेतु लकड़ी की अत्यधिक खपत से वनों का विनाश हुआ; अति-चारण से अर्ध-शुष्क भूमि बंजर हो गई।

declineTheoriesTable.proponents: Robert L. Raikes, George F. Dales, M.R. Sahni

basisAndRefutation.en: Seismic activity near Sehwan created an artificial natural dam on Indus, ponding water back and submerging Mohenjo-daro under deep silt layers (evidenced by 7 rebuild layers separated by silt beds).
basisAndRefutation.hi: सेहवान के पास भूकंप से सिन्धु नदी का प्राकृतिक बांध बन गया, जिससे मोहनजोदड़ो बार-बार जलमग्न हुआ (7 बार पुनर्निर्माण के साक्ष्य)।

declineTheoriesTable.proponents: D.P. Agrawal, R.K. Sood, B.B. Lal

basisAndRefutation.en: Tectonic shifts captured Sutlej into Indus basin and Yamuna into Ganga basin, depriving Ghaggar-Hakra of perennial Himalayan waters; major cluster of sites in Rajasthan/Haryana desiccated, triggering eastward migration.
basisAndRefutation.hi: भूगर्भिक हलचलों से सतलज सिन्धु में और यमुना गंगा में मिल गई; घग्घर-हाकरा सूख गई और आबादी गंगा-यमुना दोआब की ओर पलायन कर गई।

declineTheoriesTable.proponents: Gurdeep Singh (Pollen Study), 4.2 Kiloyear Event Studies

basisAndRefutation.en: Pollen analysis of Sambhar and Lunkaransar lakes proved sharp decline in rainfall ~2000 BCE; global 4.2 kiloyear BP megadrought weakened Southwest monsoon, devastating rainfed agriculture.
basisAndRefutation.hi: सांभर झील के परागकण अध्ययन से सिद्ध हुआ कि 2000 ई.पू. के आसपास वर्षा में भारी गिरावट आई; 4.2 किलोवर्ष महासूखे से कृषि नष्ट हो गई।

basisAndRefutation.en: Bio-archaeological analysis of skeletons from Mohenjo-daro and Harappa revealed porotic hyperostosis, severe anemia, and endemic malaria due to stagnating canal waters.
basisAndRefutation.hi: मोहनजोदड़ो व हड़प्पा के कंकालों के जैव-पुरातात्विक परीक्षण से गंभीर रक्ताल्पता और रुके हुए पानी से फैले मलेरिया के प्रमाण मिले।

basisAndRefutation.en: Collapse of Akkadian empire (~2150 BCE) sharply reduced Mesopotamian demand for lapis lazuli, carnelian, and ivory; de-urbanized Harappan trade craft guild economies.
basisAndRefutation.hi: अक्कादियन साम्राज्य के पतन (~2150 ई.पू.) से मेसोपोटामिया में भारतीय विलासिता वस्तुओं की मांग समाप्त हो गई, जिससे नगर व्यवस्था लड़खड़ा गई।

examTraps.fact: Harappans were Chalcolithic / Bronze Age people. Iron was COMPLETELY UNKNOWN to them. Iron first appeared in India during the Later Vedic period (~1000 BCE) at Atranjikhera (Etah, UP) and Gandhara.

examTraps.trap: Lion vs Tiger Seal Trap (शेर बनाम बाघ)
examTraps.fact: Tiger is frequently depicted on Indus seals (including horned deities fighting tigers and human-tiger hybrids). LION WAS NEVER DEPICTED on any Indus seal or terracotta object.
Humped Bull (Zebu) was the most sacred animal and Unicorn was the most frequent motif (>70%). COW WAS NEVER DEPICTED on Indus seals or stone seals (though domesticated biologically).

examTraps.trap: Temple & Public Religion Trap (मंदिर एवं पूजा स्थल)
examTraps.fact: NO MONUMENTAL TEMPLE or dedicated public worship building has ever been discovered in the entire IVC (in stark contrast to contemporary Sumerian Ziggurats and Egyptian stone temples).

NO METALLIC COINS existed in IVC. Trade was conducted strictly through barter and regulated by standardized cubical chert weights based on binary and decimal ratios. First punched-marked coins (Aahat) appeared much later in ~6th century BCE.

examTraps.trap: Cotton Priority Trap (कपास का प्रथम उत्पादन)
examTraps.fact: Harappans were the FIRST PEOPLE IN THE WORLD to cultivate, spin and weave cotton (called 'Sindhu' in Akkadian and 'Sindon' in Greek derived from Sindh). It did NOT originate in Egypt.
Harappan script is Boustrophedon (written from Right to Left in the first line, and Left to Right in the second line). It is logo-syllabic with ~400-450 signs (most common is the Fish symbol).
Rakhigarhi (Haryana, >350–550 hectares) is now officially confirmed as the LARGEST Harappan site in the world, surpassing Mohenjo-daro (~300 hectares). Largest site in Gujarat is Dholavira.

masterMnemonics.title: Geographical Extremes (भौगोलिक सीमाएं)
masterMnemonics.text: Manda (North, Chenab) -> Sutkagan Dor (West, Dasht) -> Daimabad (South, Pravara) -> Alamgirpur (East, Hindon).

masterMnemonics.title: Pashupati Mahadeva 4 Wild Animals (पशुपति मुहर के 4 पशु)
masterMnemonics.text: Elephant (हाथी), Tiger (बाघ), Rhinoceros (गेंडा), Buffalo (भैंसा) surrounding the seated deity + 2 Deers (हिरण) grazing below his throne.

masterMnemonics.title: Harappan Sites in Uttar Pradesh (उत्तर प्रदेश के 5 स्थल)
City Planning Exceptions (नगर नियोजन अपवाद)
masterMnemonics.text: D-3: Dholavira is divided into 3 PARTS (Citadel, Middle Town, Lower Town). C-0: Chanhudaro has 0 CITADEL (only unfortified craft town).

masterMnemonics.title: Earliest Rice Evidence (चावल के प्राचीनतम साक्ष्य)
masterMnemonics.text: Rangpur and Lothal both yielded rice husks embedded in ceramic matrices in Gujarat.

uppscRoAro.syllabusWeightage: 1 to 2 direct objective questions in Preliminary Exam (Paper 1 General Studies, 140 Marks); 1 compulsory question (8 Marks short or 12 Marks long) frequently asked in Mains Paper 1 (General Studies, 200 Marks).

prelimsPyqs.qEn: Which of the following Harappan sites is located in Uttar Pradesh?
prelimsPyqs.qHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा हड़प्पा कालीन स्थल उत्तर प्रदेश में स्थित है?

explanation.en: Hulas is located in Saharanpur district of Uttar Pradesh. Banawali is in Haryana, Kalibangan in Rajasthan, and Dholavira in Gujarat.
explanation.hi: हुलास उत्तर प्रदेश के सहारनपुर जिले में स्थित है। बनावली हरियाणा में, कालीबंगा राजस्थान में तथा धौलावीरा गुजरात में स्थित है।

prelimsPyqs.qEn: At which of the following Harappan sites has the earliest evidence of a ploughed field been discovered?
prelimsPyqs.qHi: निम्नलिखित में से किस हड़प्पा कालीन स्थल से जुते हुए खेत के प्राचीनतम साक्ष्य मिले हैं?

explanation.en: The ploughed agricultural field with criss-cross furrows was excavated at Kalibangan (Hanumangarh, Rajasthan) by B.B. Lal and B.K. Thapar.
explanation.hi: कालीबंगा (राजस्थान) में ग्रिड पद्धति पर जुते हुए खेत के साक्ष्य मिले हैं, जहां एक साथ दो फसलें (चना और सरसों) उगाई जाती थीं।

prelimsPyqs.qEn: The famous bronze figure of a 'Dancing Girl' was discovered from which Harappan site?
prelimsPyqs.qHi: प्रसिद्ध कांस्य नर्तकी की मूर्ति निम्नलिखित में से किस हड़प्पा स्थल से प्राप्त हुई थी?

explanation.en: The 10.5 cm bronze Dancing Girl cast using the lost-wax technique was discovered at Mohenjo-daro in 1926 by Ernest Mackay in the HR area.
explanation.hi: 10.5 सेमी की कांस्य नर्तकी की प्रतिमा मोहनजोदड़ो (लरकाना, सिंध) से 1926 में अर्नेस्ट मैके द्वारा प्राप्त की गई थी।

prelimsPyqs.qEn: Which of the following animals was NOT represented on the seals and terracotta art of the Harappan culture?
prelimsPyqs.qHi: निम्नलिखित पशुओं में से किस एक का हड़प्पा संस्कृति की मुहरों और टेराकोटा कलाकृतियों में अंकन नहीं मिलता है?

explanation.en: The Cow was never depicted on Harappan seals or terracotta art. Elephant, Rhinoceros, Tiger, and Humped Bull were prominently featured.
explanation.hi: हड़प्पा कालीन मुहरों पर गाय का अंकन नहीं मिलता है, जबकि हाथी, गेंडा, बाघ, वृषभ व काल्पनिक एकशृंगी (यूनिकॉर्न) का प्रचुर अंकन है।

prelimsPyqs.qEn: Which Harappan city is uniquely divided into three major sectors?
prelimsPyqs.qHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा हड़प्पा नगर विशिष्ट रूप से तीन प्रमुख भागों में विभाजित था?

explanation.en: Dholavira in Kutch, Gujarat is divided into three parts: Citadel, Middle Town, and Lower Town, unlike other Indus cities which were divided into two parts.
explanation.hi: गुजरात के कच्छ जिले में स्थित धौलावीरा तीन भागों (दुर्ग, मध्यम नगर तथा निचला नगर) में विभाजित एकमात्र नगर था।

mainsQuestions.qEn: Highlight the distinctive salient features of the town planning and underground drainage system of the Indus Valley Civilization.
mainsQuestions.qHi: सिन्धु घाटी सभ्यता के नगर नियोजन एवं भूमिगत जल निकासी प्रणाली की प्रमुख विशेषताओं को रेखांकित कीजिए।

modelAnswer.en: The Harappan town planning showcased unprecedented municipal engineering: (1) Gridiron / Chessboard Layout: Streets intersected at strict right angles (90 degrees), dividing cities into rectangular blocks oriented along cardinal directions. (2) Dual Division: Raised Western Citadel housed administrative and granary complexes; Eastern Lower Town accommodated common residential quarters (Dholavira uniquely had 3 tiers). (3) Standardized Bricks: Kiln-baked bricks in uniform 1:2:4 ratio laid in English bond masonry with gypsum mortar. (4) Underground Drainage: Waste water from house bathrooms flowed into covered street sewers equipped with inspection sumps and terracotta soak jars, covered with removable limestone slabs. (5) Introverted Architecture: House entrances opened into side lanes rather than main streets to ensure privacy and eliminate noise.
modelAnswer.hi: हड़प्पा सभ्यता का नगर नियोजन समकालीन विश्व में अद्वितीय था: (1) ग्रिड पद्धति: सड़कें समकोण (90°) पर काटती हुई नगर को आयताकार खंडों में बांटती थीं। (2) द्वि-विभाजन: पश्चिमी गढ़ी (दुर्ग) प्रशासनिक व अन्नागार हेतु तथा पूर्वी निचला नगर आवासीय बस्ती था (धौलावीरा में 3 स्तर)। (3) मानकीकृत ईंटें: 1:2:4 अनुपात की पकी ईंटें जिप्सम गारे के साथ प्रयुक्त हुईं। (4) भूमिगत जल निकासी: घरों की नालियां ढकी हुई मुख्य नालियों में मिलती थीं, जिनमें गाद रोकने हेतु सोक-पिट व निरीक्षण गड्ढे थे। (5) आवासीय निजता: मुख्य सड़क पर कोई खिड़की या सीधा प्रवेश द्वार नहीं खुलता था, द्वार गलियों में खुलते थे।

mainsQuestions.evaluationRubric: Grid system & 1:2:4 bricks (2M) | Covered drainage & soak jars (3M) | Citadel vs Lower Town & domestic privacy (3M)

mainsQuestions.qEn: Discuss the archaeological significance of Harappan sites discovered in Uttar Pradesh with special reference to Sanauli and Alamgirpur.
mainsQuestions.qHi: सनौली एवं आलमगीरपुर के विशेष संदर्भ में उत्तर प्रदेश में खोजे गए हड़प्पा स्थलों के पुरातात्विक महत्व की विवेचना कीजिए।

modelAnswer.en: Harappan sites in western Uttar Pradesh demonstrate the eastern expansion and transitional evolution of the civilization into the Ganga-Yamuna Doab: (1) Alamgirpur (Meerut): Discovered on Hindon River, marking the easternmost geographical boundary of IVC; yielded textile impressions on ceramic troughs. (2) Sanauli (Baghpat): Yielded 125+ graves containing world's earliest copper-plated solid-wheel royal war chariots, copper antennae swords, warrior shields, and ornate anthropomorphic coffins, proving military sophistication. (3) Mandi (Muzaffarnagar): Unearthed an immense hoard of Harappan gold jewellery and micro-beads. (4) Hulas (Saharanpur): Showed agricultural diversification with evidence of 5 crops (wheat, barley, rice, ragi, moong). These sites illustrate the synthesis between Late Harappan culture and the indigenous Copper Hoard/OCP horizon.
modelAnswer.hi: पश्चिमी उत्तर प्रदेश के हड़प्पा स्थल सभ्यता के पूर्वगामी प्रसार और गंगा-यमुना दोआब में संक्रमण को दर्शाते हैं: (1) आलमगीरपुर (मेरठ): हिण्डन नदी पर स्थित यह सिन्धु सभ्यता का सबसे पूर्वी छोर है; यहाँ सूती वस्त्र की छाप व बर्तन मिले हैं। (2) सनौली (बागपत): 125+ कब्रों के उत्खनन से तांबे से मढ़े युद्ध रथ, एंटीनी तलवारें, ढालें व ताम्र-जड़ित ताबूत मिले, जो उन्नत युद्ध कौशल प्रमाणित करते हैं। (3) मांडी (मुजफ्फरनगर): विशाल स्वर्ण आभूषण व सूक्ष्म मणकों का खजाना प्राप्त हुआ। (4) हुलास (सहारनपुर): 5 फसलों (गेहूं, जौ, चावल, रागी, मूंग) के प्रमाण मिले। ये स्थल उत्तर हड़प्पा और गैरिक मृद्भांड (OCP) के समन्वय के प्रतीक हैं।

mainsQuestions.evaluationRubric: Alamgirpur easternmost boundary (2M) | Sanauli royal chariots & weaponry (3M) | Mandi & Hulas findings (2M) | Synthesis with OCP (1M)

mainsQuestions.qEn: Critically examine the major theories regarding the decline of the Indus Valley Civilization. Was it a sudden catastrophic collapse or a gradual transformation?
mainsQuestions.qHi: सिन्धु घाटी सभ्यता के पतन से संबंधित प्रमुख सिद्धांतों का आलोचनात्मक परीक्षण कीजिए। क्या यह आकस्मिक विनाश था अथवा क्रमिक परिवर्तन?

modelAnswer.en: The decline of the Indus Valley Civilization (c. 1900 BCE) represents one of the most debated questions in Indian proto-history: (1) Aryan Invasion Theory: Proposed by Wheeler and Childe citing Rigvedic 'Purandara' and Mohenjo-daro skeletons. This has been decisively refuted by Kennedy and Dales as skeletons show anemia/malaria, not trauma, and a 300-year gap separates IVC decline from Vedic migration. (2) Ecological & Climatic Shift: Fairservis emphasized deforestation from over-firing baked bricks. Recent speleothem data confirms the 4.2 kiloyear BP global megadrought that weakened monsoons across South Asia. (3) Hydrological Instability: Raikes and Sahni posited tectonic uplifts damming the Indus; Agrawal and Lal highlighted the desiccation of the sacred Saraswati (Ghaggar-Hakra) river system as Sutlej and Yamuna shifted away. (4) Economic Disruption: Ratnagar demonstrated that the collapse of Mesopotamian trade disrupted urban craft networks. Conclusion: Modern consensus rejects a single apocalyptic collapse. Instead, climate aridification and hydrological shifts caused gradual de-urbanization, decentralization, and eastward migration of populations into agrarian settlements of Punjab, Haryana, and western UP.
modelAnswer.hi: हड़प्पा सभ्यता का पतन (लगभग 1900 ई.पू.) आकस्मिक विनाश न होकर क्रमिक वि-नगरीकरण एवं रूपांतरण था: (1) आर्य आक्रमण सिद्धांत: व्हीलर व चाइल्ड ने ऋग्वेद में इंद्र को 'पुरंदर' कहे जाने व मोहनजोदड़ो के कंकालों के आधार पर यह सिद्धांत दिया। केनेडी व डेल्स ने इसे पूर्णतः खंडित किया क्योंकि कंकालों पर युद्ध के घाव नहीं बल्कि मलेरिया/एनीमिया के साक्ष्य हैं तथा कालक्रम में 300 वर्षों का अंतर है। (2) जलवायु एवं पारिस्थितिक क्षरण: फेयरसर्विस के अनुसार ईंट पकाने हेतु वनों के अंधाधुंध कटान से पर्यावरण असंतुलन हुआ। 4.2 किलोवर्ष महासूखे ने मानसूनी वर्षा को अत्यधिक कमजोर कर दिया। (3) भूगर्भीय व जलप्लावन परिवर्तन: रेइक्स के अनुसार विवर्तनिक हलचलों से सिन्धु में बाढ़ आई; अग्रवाल व लाल के अनुसार घग्घर-हाकरा (सरस्वती) नदी सूख गई क्योंकि सतलज सिन्धु की ओर और यमुना गंगा की ओर मुड़ गई। (4) व्यापारिक पतन: रत्नागर के अनुसार मेसोपोटामियाई व्यापार टूटने से नगरीय शिल्प आधार ढह गया। निष्कर्ष: यह आकस्मिक पतन नहीं बल्कि जलवायु परिवर्तन व नदी मार्ग बदलाव के कारण पूर्व (गंगा-यमुना दोआब) व दक्षिण की ओर हुआ क्रमिक ग्रामीण विस्थापन था।

mainsQuestions.evaluationRubric: Wheeler invasion theory & refutation (3M) | Climatic drought & hydrological shift (4M) | Trade collapse & ecological factors (3M) | Balanced synthesis: transformation not collapse (2M)

mainsQuestions.qEn: Analyze the socio-religious practices and craft specialization of Harappan people based on archaeological artifacts recovered from major sites.
mainsQuestions.qHi: प्रमुख स्थलों से प्राप्त पुरातात्विक पुरावशेषों के आधार पर हड़प्पा कालीन सामाजिक-धार्मिक मान्यताओं एवं शिल्प विशेषज्ञता का विश्लेषण कीजिए।

modelAnswer.en: Archaeological artifacts reveal a sophisticated, stratified, and non-theocratic socio-religious structure: (1) Religious Practices: (a) Female Fertility Cult: Terracotta Mother Goddess figurines with fan-shaped headdresses prominent at Harappa and Mohenjo-daro (absent at Lothal/Kalibangan). (b) Male Divinity: Pashupati Mahadeva seal depicting a proto-Shiva seated in yogic posture with horned headgear, surrounded by elephant, tiger, rhino, buffalo. (c) Aniconic & Natural Worship: Phallic linga and yoni stones; worship of Pipal tree and sacred animals (Zebu humped bull, mythical Unicorn). (d) Water & Fire Rituals: Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro for public lustrations; rows of Fire Altars (Yajna-kundas) at Kalibangan and Lothal. (e) Absence of Temples: No public temples or priestly kingly palaces found. (2) Craft Specialization: (a) Metallurgy: Lost-wax (cire perdue) bronze casting (Dancing Girl, Daimabad chariot Hoard). (b) Bead Making: Chanhudaro and Lothal factories produced micro-beads from agate, carnelian, and steatite using specialized bronze drills. (c) Standardized Weights: Binary (1, 2, 4, 8, 16) and decimal system based on cubical chert weights.
modelAnswer.hi: पुरातात्विक पुरावशेष हड़प्पा समाज की बहुआयामी व समतामूलक प्रकृति को प्रमाणित करते हैं: (1) धार्मिक जीवन: (क) मातृदेवी पूजा: पंखेनुमा शिरोभूषा वाली मिट्टी की मातृदेवी मूर्तियां (हड़प्पा व मोहनजोदड़ो में प्रमुख, लोथल/कालीबंगा में अनुपस्थित)। (ख) पशुपति शिव: योग मुद्रा में त्रिमुखी सींगधारी देव, जिसके चारों ओर हाथी, बाघ, गेंडा व भैंसा तथा पैरों के पास 2 हिरण हैं। (ग) प्रकृति व प्रतीक पूजा: पीपल वृक्ष, एकशृंगी (यूनिकॉर्न) व कूबड़दार वृषभ की पूजा; लिंग-योनि पूजा के पाषाण प्रतीक। (घ) अग्नि व जल कर्मकांड: मोहनजोदड़ो का विशाल स्नानागार (सामूहिक शुद्धि स्नान) तथा कालीबंगा व लोथल की अग्निवेदियां (यज्ञ कुंड)। (ङ) मंदिर विहीन समाज: किसी मंदिर या पुरोहिती राजप्रासाद का कोई साक्ष्य नहीं। (2) शिल्प विशेषज्ञता: (क) धातु विज्ञान: भ्रष्ट मोम पद्धति (Lost-wax) से बनी कांस्य नर्तकी व दैमाबाद का रथ। (ख) मणका निर्माण: चन्हूदड़ो व लोथल के कारखानों में सेलखड़ी, गोमेद व कार्नेलियन के सूक्ष्म मणके ड्रिल द्वारा बनाए गए। (ग) मानकीकृत बाट: 16 के गुणज (बाइनरी) एवं दशमलव आधारित घनाकार चर्ट बाट।

mainsQuestions.evaluationRubric: Pashupati & Mother Goddess (3M) | Fire altars & Great Bath ritualism (3M) | Absence of temples (2M) | Craft, metallurgy & bead-making specialization (4M)
